Given A project parameter defines a requirement or constraint (or a project that can be defined before any file imports or design actions. What is an example of a project parameter commonly available in WLAN design software?
Minimum required signal strength is a project parameter because it defines a measurable RF acceptance threshold that the design must meet in each applicable requirement area.
In most WLAN design tools, after defining project parameters or during the project creation wizard what action will you take before you can begin the actual design process?
Importing the floor plan gives the design tool the building geometry on which to place APs, define walls and requirement areas, and model RF propagation.
What is the purpose of defining wall materials in WLAN design software?
To ensure the attenuation and reflection of the materials are considered during propagation modeling
So that the floor plan looks as much like the target deployment space as possible
It adds color to the floor plan which makes it easier to identify requirement areas
Manager require it, so WLAN designers should do it.
Adding wall materials and their attenuation/reflection properties lets predictive software model how the building changes RF propagation instead of treating the floor plan as open space.
To ensure that your design meets the requirements of the WLAN, what should be defined in your WLAN design software that will result in different requirements at varying locations on the floor plan1?
Requirement areas let the designer assign different signal, SNR, capacity, or application requirements to different parts of the floor plan.
When performing a spectrum analysis walkthrough of a facility tor which you will be creating a WLAN design you detect an interferer What should you do?
Make a mental note of it so that you can include it in your design
Make note of it using the reporting features of your spectrum analyzer or by documenting it elsewhere
Locate and remove the interferer immediately so that your WLAN works well
Walk away from the project because it is best to only deploy in clean environments with no other RF signals
Document the detected interferer, including its frequency, location, and observed behavior. The designer can then account for it in channel planning and the final design report.

While using a USB adapter attached to a USB hub and your laptop for protocol analysts you notice that the SNR is lower than expected. The USB adapter is an 802.11 ac 3x3 3 adapter and is connected to a USB 3 hub. What is likely causing the SNR variation?
EMI from the battery in the device
RF incidental energy generated by the cooling fans in the laptop
Some USB 3.0 devices and cables emit broadband noise around 2.4 GHz. That can raise the apparent noise floor and distort survey measurements.
When implementing multiple SSIDs to what is each SSID typically mapped in order to provide traffic management separately for each SSID?
Mapping an SSID to a VLAN gives that WLAN service a logical Layer 2 segment and allows wired network policies to be applied to its traffic.

An organization is implementing a new WLAN. They are upgrading a very old 802.11g network that only a few devices used Now. they expect more than 250 devices to use the new WLAN that will operate 802.11ax Aps. What wired-side consideration should you address in your design recommendations?
A WLAN with many clients needs enough DHCP addresses and appropriate lease management so address exhaustion does not prevent new associations from obtaining IP connectivity.

You are designing a WLAN and have been asked to recommend a security solution for the network The organization requires that 802 1X/EAP be implemented, but they do not have a PKI and do not wish to deploy one They suggest that mostly Windows clients. Apple phones and Android phones will be used What do you recommend?
Use CCMP AES with a PSK
Use EAP-PEAP for the authentication solution
Use FAP-TLS for the authentication solution
PEAP authenticates the server with a certificate, then carries the user's inner credentials through the protected TLS tunnel. It is suitable when a client PKI is not available.
You must perform a site survey that defines signal strength, throughput and latency What kind of survey should you perform?
Perform a passive survey using a laptop's built-in wireless adapter
Perform a passive survey using a USB wireless adapter
Perform an active survey using a laptop's built-in adapter
Perform a passive survey using a special monitor mode adapter
An active survey associates to the WLAN and generates traffic, allowing validation of application performance and client roaming behavior.

An organization has chosen to implement Wi-Fi 6E and operates in a regulatory domain allowing the use of all 6 GHz channels. Why can 40 MHz channels be used more easily in this network than one operating in the 5 GHz band?
Because ACI works differently in 6 GHz than in 5 GHz
Because many more channels are available
Because Wi-Fi 6E supports 40 MHz as a primary channel and ignores 20 MHz primary channels
Because 6 GHz Wi-Fi uses Single Channel Architecture instead of Multiple Channel Architecture
The 6 GHz band offers many more channels than 2.4 or 5 GHz, so 40 MHz channel planning has more room for reuse and fewer constraints from channel scarcity.
What is a typical characteristic of barcode scanners?
No support for any 802.11 security solutions
Barcode scanners typically exchange small inventory or transaction messages, so their throughput demand is modest; coverage, latency, and roaming may matter more.
What document can be useful when determining client capabilities in a WLAN design project?
A client specification sheet identifies supported bands, channels, spatial streams, channel widths, and security features, which are essential inputs to a compatibility-focused WLAN design.
What inexpensive tool is capable of locating neighbor WLANs if that is your only need?
A WLAN scanner passively discovers nearby APs and reports attributes such as SSID, BSSID, channel, security, and received signal level.
What are the two most common industry-standard protocols used to transport data from an AP to a Wireless LAN Controller?
CAPWAP and GRE are commonly used tunneling mechanisms to carry AP traffic or control/data traffic toward a WLAN controller.
Which one of the following options is a dedicated throughput testing application, usable on both the WLAN and LAN?
iPerf is a dedicated tool for generating TCP/UDP traffic and measuring throughput between endpoints. The PDF appears to contain an OCR typo in the option text.
What is the most appropriate antenna which will require the least Intentional Radiator power for a point-to-point bridge link spanning 1200 meters?
A directional dish with the specified gain concentrates RF energy toward the remote endpoint, allowing the required link budget with less transmitter power.
What commonly used item can help to prevent back pain during lengthy site surveys?
A survey tray distributes the weight of a laptop and survey equipment, reducing strain during long walk-throughs.
Which type of building material causes the most attenuation of Wi-Fi signals'?
Fire-rated steel doors are dense metal barriers and can cause substantial RF attenuation compared with typical interior wall materials.
What are the best practices for better location accuracy when deploying Wi-Fi RTLS?
Place APs on the center of the required area and make sure that every client device is able to hear at least three APs
Place APs on the perimeter and throughout the required area and make sure that every client device is able to hear at least three APs
Place APs on the center of the required area and make sure that every client device is able to hear at least two APs
Place APs on the perimeter of the required area and make sure that every client device is able to hear at least one AP
For Wi-Fi RTLS, multiple APs should hear each client from different positions. Perimeter and interior placement improves geometry and supports more reliable location estimates.
